content_html:
Peru is a must-see destination for food lovers. Its diversity of ingredients and the fusion of cultural influences have made its cuisine one of the most recognized worldwide. Throughout the year, the country celebrates various gastronomic festivities where you can try the best of its seasoning. Here we present some of the most important ones.

1. Mistura (Lima) – October (variable date)

It is the largest gastronomic fair in Peru and Latin America. For several days, the best chefs and traditional cooks meet in Lima to offer a wide variety of typical dishes. From ceviche and anticuchos to desserts like suspiro a la limeña, Mistura is a must-visit festival for lovers of Peruvian food.

2. Ceviche Festival (Lima) – June 28

Ceviche, Peru's flagship dish, has its own festival on June 28, the date on which the National Ceviche Day. In different cities of the country, especially in Lima and the coast, restaurants and gastronomic fairs offer traditional and creative versions of this iconic dish based on fish, lemon, chili and onion.

3. Peruvian Cuisine Week (Entire country) – October

During this week, restaurants and markets throughout the country celebrate the richness of Peruvian gastronomy with promotions and special menus. It is an excellent opportunity to try different dishes and learn more about the culinary diversity of each region.

4. Chancho al Palo Festival (Huaral) – October

In the province of Huaral, about two hours from Lima, this festival is held dedicated to one of the most delicious dishes of the Peruvian mountains and coast: pig on the stick. This slow-cooked wood-fired pork is a crispy, juicy delicacy that attracts thousands of visitors every year.

5. Cheese and Milk Festival (Cajamarca) – February

Cajamarca, famous for its dairy products, celebrates this festival in February. During the event, you can taste various types of cheeses, butters and desserts made with fresh milk, in addition to enjoying contests and craft fairs.

6. Pachamanca Festival (Huancayo) – August

Pachamanca is an Andean dish prepared in an underground oven with hot stones. At this festival, held in August in Huancayo, visitors can experience this traditional cooking technique and try slow-cooked varieties of meat, potatoes, and Andean herbs.

7. Pisco Sour Festival (Lima and the entire country) – First Saturday of February

On the first Saturday in February, tribute is paid to the Pisco Sour, the most emblematic cocktail of Peru. During this day, bars and restaurants offer tastings, promotions and shows related to this drink based on pisco, lemon, sugar and egg white.

8. Cuy Festival (Huacho and Cusco) – Variable date

Cuy is one of the most traditional meats in the Peruvian mountains. Festivals dedicated to this dish are held in several regions of the country, highlighting Huacho and Cusco, where you can try different versions of fried, baked or stewed guinea pig.

Enjoy your trip!!!
